title: Normal projective Galois envelope of a separable alteration
statement: Let $S$ be an excellent integral Noetherian scheme with function field $K$, and let $r:V\to S$ be a proper surjective morphism with $V$ integral, finite over a dense open of $S$, such that $k(V)/K$ is finite separable. There exist a finite Galois extension $L/K$ containing $k(V)$, a normal integral excellent Noetherian scheme $W$ with $k(W)=L$, a surjective morphism $c:W\to S$ which is projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], and an $S$-morphism $t:W\to V$. The finite group $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(L)$ acts on $W$ over $S$, inducing its given action on the function field. There is a dense open $U\subset S$ such that $c^{-1}U\to U$ is a finite etale $G$-torsor, meaning finite etale and surjective with a simply transitive $G$-action on every geometric fibre. In particular $c$ is finite over a dense open and generically etale. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. Function fields have the meaning of [def-sc-function-field]; finite Galois means finite, normal and separable as a field extension, with fixed field $L^G=K$.

source.place: Exposé X Theorem 3.4 proof Step 4, printed pp. 160--161: replace the separable alteration by a dominating separable projective Galois alteration and normalize. Definition 3.3.1, printed p.158, specifies the generic Galois condition. The projective domination is the usual Chow preparation, conjugate-product model and finite normalization over an excellent base, not a prime-to-ell claim.

proof.text: Write $E=k(V)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-chow-noetherian] to $V\to S$. Its hypotheses hold because proper morphisms are separated of finite type and $S$ is Noetherian. Obtain $P'\to V$, an immersion $P'\to\mathbf P^n_S$, and a dense open $V_0\subset V$ on which $P'\to V$ is an isomorphism. These data also satisfy the hypotheses of [det-chow-projective-closed-immersions], so the immersion into projective space is closed. Replace $P'$ by the reduced closed subscheme $P$ on the closure of $V_0$, using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. The closure of the integral open $V_0$ is irreducible; its reduced structure is integral and still has function field $E$. The restricted map $P\to V$ is proper and has dense image, hence is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image]. Thus $P$ has a closed embedding into $\mathbf P^n_S$ and an $S$-map to $V$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions] to the single finite separable extension $E/K$. Fix the resulting embedding $E\hookrightarrow L$, with $L/K$ finite Galois, and put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_K(L)$. The tensor decomposition of [lem-exc-finite-galois-tensor-decomposition] in particular implies that $G$ is finite: $L\otimes_KL$ is finite dimensional over $L$, whereas a product of infinitely many nonzero copies of $L$ cannot be. Also [lem-exc-etale-galois-fixed-field-subgroup], with intermediate field $K$, gives $L^G=K$.

Let $Y\to P$ be the normalization in $\operatorname{Spec}L$ at the generic point of $P$. The statement of [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension] gives an integral normal $Y$ with generic field $L$, and [def-fin-normalization-extension] identifies its charts as the integral closures of affine coordinate domains of $P$ in $L$. These charts glue by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-commutes-localization]. On every affine chart of $P$ above an affine of $S$, the coordinate ring is excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. It is Nagata by [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata], hence N-2 by [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-domain-n2]. By the definition [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], its integral closure in the finite extension $L/E$ is a finite module. Thus $Y\to P$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

proof.text: Form the finite products $D=\prod_{g\in G,S}P$ and $B=\prod_{g\in G,S}Y$, using [def-pc-fibre-product]. There is a finite morphism $B\to D$: over an affine product chart its algebra is the tensor product of the finite algebras for $Y\to P$, and tensors of their finite module generators generate it. This also proves finiteness under the base changes and compositions involved, directly from [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The product of the closed embeddings $P\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ is closed: on product affine charts its ideal is the sum of the extended defining ideals. Iterating [lem-chow-segre] therefore embeds $D$ as a closed subscheme of a single $\mathbf P^N_S$.

source.place: Segre embedding; affine tensor descriptions of finite products

proof.text: The generic fibre $P_K$ is $\operatorname{Spec}E$. Indeed $P$ is integral and birational to $V$; after base change to $K$ it is a proper integral scheme with algebraic function field $E/K$, hence has only its generic point: on an affine chart its coordinate domain is a finite type $K$-subalgebra of the finite dimensional field $E$, therefore is a field. Its field of fractions is $E$. Likewise $Y_K=\operatorname{Spec}L$, by the integral-closure localization statement in step 3. Consequently $D_K=\operatorname{Spec}(\bigotimes_{g\in G,K}E)$ and $B_K=\operatorname{Spec}(\bigotimes_{g\in G,K}L)$. Define $j:\operatorname{Spec}L\to B$ by taking in coordinate $g$ the generic inclusion $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Y$ precomposed with $\operatorname{Spec}g$. Its generic ring map is $\bigotimes_g L\to L$, $\bigotimes_g x_g\mapsto\prod_g g(x_g)$; this is surjective since the identity factor already maps onto $L$. Thus its image is a closed point $b$ of $B_K$ with residue field exactly $L$.

source.place: Normalization localization and the affine generic-fibre calculation

proof.text: Let $Z$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{\{b\}}\subset B$, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is integral. Moreover $Z_K=\operatorname{Spec}L$: on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $B$ containing $b$, its ideal is the prime kernel of $R\to L$; localization at the nonzero functions from the base commutes with this kernel and gives the kernel of the surjective generic ring map of step 5. The closure has no other points over $K$, because $b$ is closed in $B_K$. In particular $k(Z)=L$. Since $Z\to B$ is a closed immersion it is finite: its affine algebra is a quotient generated as a module by $1$. Hence $Z\to D$ is finite by the module-generator calculation of step 4. Projection to the identity factor gives an $S$-map $Z\to Y\to P\to V$.

There is a left $G$-action on $B$ by permuting coordinates: $(a_hx)_g=x_{h^{-1}g}$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives actual scheme automorphisms with $a_ha_k=a_{hk}$. On the generic point map, $a_hj=j\operatorname{Spec}(h^{-1})$, as one checks after every projection: on coordinate rings both composites send $x$ in factor $g$ to $h^{-1}(g(x))$. Thus every $a_h$ fixes $b$ as a point and preserves its closure. Uniqueness of the reduced closed structure in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] restricts these automorphisms to $Z$, preserving the group laws. Under $k(Z)=L$ their pullbacks are $h^{-1}$; equivalently the usual left action on rational functions, $h\cdot f=(a_{h^{-1}})^*f$, is the given action $h(f)$.

source.place: Fibre-product universal property and Tag 01J3, uniqueness of reduced closed structure

proof.text:
The schemes $D,B,Z$ are finite type over the excellent Noetherian scheme $S$: $D$ is closed in finite projective space, $B	o D$ is finite, and $Z	o B$ is closed. On affine charts [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] give excellence and local Noetherianity; all these schemes are quasi-compact since their displayed structural maps are quasi-compact and $S$ is quasi-compact. Let $
u:W=Z^
u	o Z$ be the normalization [def-sc-normalization]. Apply [lem-per-excellent-normalization-preparation]: $
u$ is finite and surjective, and $W$ is excellent Noetherian and normal. As $Z$ is integral, its componentwise normalization has one integral component and agrees with this function-field normalization. Localization of the integral closure at the generic point gives $k(W)=k(Z)=L$. The composite $W	o D$ is finite, and projection gives the required $t:W	o V$.

The finite map $W\to D$ is projective in the projective-bundle sense by [lem-trf-finite-projective-bundle]. The closed embedding $D\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_S$ is also a projective-bundle embedding, taking the free module $\mathcal O_S^{N+1}$ in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. Since the Noetherian scheme $S$ is qcqs, [lem-per-projective-bundle-composition] proves that $c:W\to S$ is projective in precisely the required convention. It is proper by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper]. Its image is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] and contains the generic point of $S$, since its generic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}L$. As $S$ is integral, this image is all of $S$.

For $h\in G$, apply [lem-sbc-normalization-dominant-lift] to the dominant map $a_h
u:W	o Z$. It gives a unique dominant lift $\widetilde a_h:W	o W$ satisfying $
u\widetilde a_h=a_h
u$. The identity lift is $1_W$. Both $\widetilde a_h\widetilde a_k$ and $\widetilde a_{hk}$ lift $a_{hk}
u$, so uniqueness makes them equal. Taking $k=h^{-1}$ proves that the lifts are automorphisms. They are over $S$ and have the same generic pullbacks $h^{-1}$, hence the same given left function-field action, as in step 7.

Choose a nonempty affine open $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$; it is dense because $S$ is integral. The scheme $D_{S_0}$ is H-projective and its generic fibre is the spectrum of the finite dimensional $K$-algebra $\bigotimes_G E$, hence has dimension zero. Apply [lem-fin-projective-generically-finite] and shrink to a nonempty affine open $S_1\subset S_0$ on which $D$ is finite. Because $W\to D$ is finite, $W_{S_1}$ is finite over $S_1$, by multiplying finite module generators. Write $S_1=\operatorname{Spec}A_1$ and $W_{S_1}=\operatorname{Spec}C$, where $C$ is a finite domain algebra, embedded in $L$ with $K\otimes_{A_1}C=L$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spread-finite-separable-extension] to obtain, after a principal shrinking, a finite etale domain algebra $C'$ inside $L$ with fraction field $L$. Both $C$ and $C'$ become $L$ on tensoring with $K$. Each of their finitely many module generators lies in the other algebra after inverting a nonzero element of $A_1$; invert the product of these denominators. The two localized algebras are then equal inside $L$. Thus $c$ is finite etale and still surjective over a dense affine open $S_2\subset S$.

source.place: Generic finiteness; spreading a finite separable field extension and finite-generator comparison

proof.text: Write $S_2=\operatorname{Spec}A_2$ and $W_{S_2}=\operatorname{Spec}C_2$. The torsor map $\coprod_{h\in G}W_{S_2}\to W_{S_2}\times_{S_2}W_{S_2}$, whose components are $(1,\widetilde a_h)$, corresponds to $\Phi:C_2\otimes_{A_2}C_2\to\prod_{h\in G}C_2$, $a\otimes b\mapsto(a\,h^{-1}(b))_h$. Over $K$, this is an isomorphism by [lem-exc-finite-galois-tensor-decomposition], reindexing $h$ by $h^{-1}$. The source and target of $\Phi$ are finite $A_2$-modules; its kernel is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], and its cokernel is generated by the images of the finitely many target generators. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], both become zero after localizing to $K$. Kill the finitely many generators by inverting the product of their nonzero annihilators in $A_2$. On the resulting dense open $U$, the torsor map is an isomorphism. For any geometric point of $U$, its fibre is a nonempty finite etale scheme, and the displayed isomorphism says that every ordered pair of its points is uniquely $(x,hx)$. The action on that geometric fibre is therefore simply transitive. This proves every asserted clause, without imposing any restriction on $|G|$ in the residue characteristics.
